_readme: Single source of truth for narration language/dialect options. Edit this file to tune a dialect; no code change needed. Project overrides vs the original pack: audience 9-11 (grades 4-5); no diacritics/tanween anywhere; numbers as words in spoken text; per-dialect tts_language and forbidden_words (used by the validator).

egyptian.label: Egyptian Arabic (colloquial)
egyptian.narration: Write all spoken narration (story_script, voice_script) and character dialogue in natural colloquial Egyptian Arabic, the way a warm storyteller speaks aloud to a 9-11 year old (grades 4-5).
egyptian.captions_explanations: Write captions, explanations and visual labels in simple Modern Standard Arabic that matches the textbook wording. Do not use dialect in them.
prefer: Question words: إيه، ليه، إزاي، فين، مين
Everyday particles: دلوقتي، كده، بس، خلاص، تاني
avoid: Gulf markers: وش، ليش، شلون، الحين
Heavy slang or idioms a 9-10 year old may not know
egyptian.review_note: Sample narration for this dialect comes from the project's real demo output. Project note: samples contain diacritics; they are stripped before display and TTS.

sample_narration.plant_seed_setup: زرعت مريم بذرة صغيرة في أصيص الشباك، وكانت متأكدة إنها هتشوف نبتة كبيرة الصبح. رجعت تاني يوم، فالتراب كان ساكت… لكن علامة صغيرة شقته من تحت. بصّت مريم وهمست: «مين بدأ يتحرك هناك؟»
sample_narration.friction_setup: كان ممر المدرسة هاديًا، وفجأة سمعت سلمى خشخشة عربة لعبتها. على الأرض أثران: واحد طويل والتاني أقصر. قالت: «أنا دفعت العربة… بس ليه ما كملتش نفس المسافة؟»

saudi.label: Saudi Arabic (white dialect)
saudi.narration: Write all spoken narration (story_script, voice_script) and character dialogue in natural colloquial Saudi 'white' dialect: neutral and widely understood across the Kingdom, without a strong regional (Najdi, Hijazi, Southern) accent or slang.
saudi.captions_explanations: Write captions, explanations and visual labels in simple Modern Standard Arabic that matches the textbook wording. Do not use dialect in them.
prefer: Question words: وش، ليش، كيف، وين، منو
Everyday particles: كذا، الحين، بكرة، ثاني يوم، مرّة (as intensifier)
Negation with ما + verb: ما لقت، ما مشت
avoid: Egyptian markers: ده، دي، إيه، إزاي، دلوقتي، كده، عايز
Strong regional slang or tribal/regional idioms
saudi.review_note: Sample narration for this dialect was authored by an AI model. Have a native Saudi educator review it before it is used as a reference.

sample_narration.plant_seed_setup: زرعت مريم بذرة صغيرة في الأصيص عند الشباك، وكانت متأكدة إنها بكرة بتشوف نبتة كبيرة. رجعت ثاني يوم، والتراب ساكت… بس علامة صغيرة شقّته من تحت. قربت مريم وهمست: «وش اللي يتحرك هناك؟»
sample_narration.friction_setup: كان ممر المدرسة هادي، وفجأة سمعت سلمى صوت عربتها اللعبة. على الأرض أثرين: واحد طويل وواحد أقصر. قالت: «أنا دفعت العربة… بس ليش ما مشت نفس المسافة؟»

msa.label: Modern Standard Arabic (simple, spoken-style)
msa.narration: Write all narration (story_script, voice_script) and character dialogue in simple, warm Modern Standard Arabic: short sentences, concrete verbs, everyday vocabulary and a natural storytelling rhythm. No dialect words and no heavy classical or literary vocabulary.
msa.captions_explanations: Write captions, explanations and visual labels in simple Modern Standard Arabic that matches the textbook wording.
prefer: Simple dialogue verbs: قال، همست، سأل، ابتسم
Plain unvowelled text: never write diacritics or tanween
avoid: Any colloquial words (ده، وش، ليش، إيه ...)
Lecture connectors such as: ومن الجدير بالذكر
msa.review_note: Sample narration for this dialect was authored by an AI model; review wording against the target grade.

sample_narration.plant_seed_setup: زرعت مريم بذرة صغيرة في أصيص النافذة، وكانت واثقة أنها سترى نبتة كبيرة في الصباح. وفي اليوم التالي بدا التراب ساكنًا… لكن علامة صغيرة شقّته من تحته. اقتربت مريم وهمست: «من الذي بدأ يتحرك هناك؟»
sample_narration.friction_setup: كان ممر المدرسة هادئًا، وفجأة سمعت سلمى صوت عربتها اللعبة. على الأرض أثران: أحدهما طويل والآخر أقصر. قالت: «دفعتُ العربة… فلماذا لم تقطع المسافة نفسها؟»

english.label: English
english.narration: Write all narration (story_script, voice_script) and character dialogue in simple, warm, spoken-style English for a 9-11 year old (grades 4-5): short sentences, concrete verbs, contractions allowed.
english.captions_explanations: Write captions, explanations and visual labels in plain English that matches the textbook wording.
prefer: Simple dialogue tags: said, whispered, asked
avoid: Idioms and slang a child may not know
Academic connectors such as: therefore, thus, moreover
Lecture openers such as: Today we will learn
english.review_note: Sample narration for this dialect was authored by an AI model.

sample_narration.plant_seed_setup: Maryam planted a tiny seed in the pot by the window, sure she'd see a big plant by morning. The next day the soil sat perfectly still… but a tiny mark had cracked it open from underneath. Maryam leaned in and whispered, "Who's moving down there?"
sample_narration.friction_setup: The school hallway was quiet, until Salma heard her toy cart rattle. Two marks lay on the floor: one long, one short. "I pushed it the same way," she said. "So why didn't it go as far?"

shared_rules.terminology: Technical terms, labels, units and numbers must always match the textbook exactly, whatever dialect is selected.
shared_rules.student_address_arabic: Arabic imperatives are gendered. Prefer gender-neutral phrasing (plural or 'let's' style, for example: خلّينا نجرّب / لنجرّب) instead of guessing the learner's gender. If the product knows the learner's gender, pass it explicitly as an input.
shared_rules.consistency: Use one dialect per lesson. Do not mix dialects inside a lesson or a scene.
shared_rules.json_keys: JSON keys and enum values stay in English. Only learner-facing string values use the selected language.
shared_rules.no_diacritics: Never write diacritics (tashkeel) or tanween anywhere: no fatha, damma, kasra, sukun, shadda, tanween and no tatweel. Plain unvowelled letters only.
shared_rules.spoken_numbers: All spoken text (story, narration, quiz, checks, reactions) is read aloud by a text-to-speech voice, so write every number as a word (for example خمس تفاحات, not 5). Digits and symbols are allowed only inside the SVG drawing and in lab labels.
